source.title: Exploring Visual Vulnerabilities via Multi-Loss Adversarial Search for Jailbreaking Vision-Language Models
source.authors: Shu-Yang Hao; Bryan Hooi; Jun Liu; Kai-Wei Chang; Zi Huang; Yu-Jun Cai

record.tranche_reason: The study tests visual jailbreaks in VLMs, but does not test fine-tuning, first-token KL concentration, compliant-prefixing, suffixes, decoding changes, safety-localized weights, or deepening safety training. Its visual-attack results are related to safety vulnerability but do not test the claim versions as specified.
record.gate_note: The paper reports harmful-response rates for visual attacks and image conditions. These are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version: none of the tested conditions measures the fine-tuning, token-position, or safety-localization mechanism named in the claim versions. The paper cites the original fine-tuning paper, but cited results are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The paper attacks VLMs (MiniGPT-4, LLaVA-2, plus Gemini, ChatGLM and Qwen black-box) with gradient-optimized, scenario-matched adversarial images. It has no fine-tuning (V1/V2), no aligned-vs-base per-token KL (V3), and no prefilling, text suffix or decoding manipulation (V4). It does not test weight localization (V5), causes of shallowness (V6) or deepening training (V7). The image optimization targets affirmative/harmful response text, which resembles suffix attacks. But it is an image-modality attack and the paper reports no token-position analysis, so it is a related construct, not V4 as stated. The original fine-tuning paper is cited only once, in the introduction, as a safety-protocol reference. The relation is therefore cites_only rather than discusses.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is essentially correct. The authors conclude that scenario-matched images amplify harmful outputs and that minimal-loss adversarial images are not optimal. Their MLAI attack (multi-image, flat-minima loss range) reaches 77.75% and 82.80% ASR and transfers to commercial VLMs. They propose similarity-based deduplication as a defense.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses visual adversarial-image attacks on VLMs; it does not implement the original fine-tuning or token-depth methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Attack success varies by scenario and model; the paper reports different outcomes for blank, irrelevant, and scenario-matched images, and varying outcomes across loss ranges, image counts, and ρ.

fits_no_version.finding: Scenario-matched, gradient-optimized adversarial images raise harmful-response ASR. On MiniGPT-4 it rises from 32.71% (plain text) to 77.75%; on LLaVA-2 from 39.83% to 82.80%. The images transfer to black-box VLMs at 39.84–60.11%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Visual adversarial inputs, especially semantically matched images, bypass VLM safety alignment inherited from the LLM without weight changes.

fits_no_version.finding: A similarity-based deduplication defense reduces MLAI ASR on MiniGPT-4 by 22.99%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Removing near-duplicate adversarial images reduces multi-image visual jailbreak success.

record.problems: The paper reports no uncertainty estimates. Figure-only ablation results do not provide exact ASR values in the text. The black-box table has no plain-text baseline. ASR uses a single stated judging model, Beaver-dam-7B.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 scenario-level results for Plain Text, Liu et al. [21], and Qi et al. [28] were not separately extracted because the scenario-level MLAI and aggregate comparator results were retained within the 60-row limit. Figure 2 cross-scenario transfer values, Figures 7–8 loss-range/image-count/ρ sweeps, and Figure 9 scenario-level defense bars were omitted; they concern attack configuration or are figure-only results without text-stated individual values.

untested.parts: No per-token KL or position analysis.
No prefilling, text-suffix or decoding attacks. Attacks are adversarial images, without analysis of response openings.
No test of data or objective causes of shallow safety.
No deepening training or robustness test.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not a test of any version. The closest link is V4 in spirit, since images are optimized toward affirmative/harmful target text. However, it is a different modality, with no measurement of where in the response safety fails. The single Beaver-dam-7B judge uses scenario-specific criteria. For PL/GD (avoiding political topics) and LO/FA/HC (missing disclaimers), these differ from harmful compliance, which explains the high plain-text baselines there.

versions.untested_parts: No compliant opening, adversarial suffix, or decoding-change test; attacks use images.
No weight or rank localization test.
No test of whether data or training objective produces shallow safety.
No training that deepens safety or test of whether deepening holds up.

rows.operation_detail: MLAI visual adversarial-image attack; harmfulness judged using Beaver-dam-7B
rows.note: Authors state the MLAI improvement here is 0.85%; Table 1 reports these ASRs.
rows.check: The note is misleading. The authors' 0.85% GD gain does not match Table 1: MLAI minus plain text is 7.56 points, and MLAI minus best prior is 6.10 points. Plain text 90.29 to 97.85 is a clear rise from a high baseline. Partial is better read as a ceiling effect.
